title: The Eternal Adversary
description: The accuser and adversary of Hebrew scripture, who tested Job and tempted Christ in the wilderness. Later tradition made him a rebel angel cast out of heaven who rules hell, the father of lies, who corrupts creation and turns souls against their maker.

title: The Coiled Deep
description: The twisting sea serpent of Job and the Psalms, armoured in scales that no spear can pierce and baited by no hook. Its sneezing sparks light, and the deep boils like a pot when it moves. Later ages named it a demon of envy, and a beast to be eaten at the end of days.

title: Coil Around the Sea
description: Third child of Loki and the giantess Angrboda, cast by Odin into the ocean, where he grew until he encircled the world and bit his own tail. Thor once hooked him and nearly pulled him up. At Ragnarök he lets go, floods the land, and he and Thor kill each other.

title: Angel of the Abyss
description: Known as Apollyon in Greek, the angel of the bottomless pit and king of the locust host of Revelation. His name means destruction, and his emergence heralds the opening of the abyss, unleashing locusts with scorpion tails on all who lack the seal of God.

title: Devourer of Izumo
description: An eight-headed, eight-tailed serpent whose body spanned eight valleys, with eyes red as winter cherries and moss and trees growing on its back. It devoured one daughter of an old couple every year. The storm god Susanoo made it drunk on eight vats of sake, then cut it to pieces and found a sword in its tail.

title: Gnawer of the World Root
description: A dragon who lives under the world tree Yggdrasil, gnawing at its roots with a swarm of serpents and eating the corpses of oath-breakers and murderers. A squirrel carries insults between him and the eagle in the branches. After Ragnarök, he flies up out of the dark with the dead on his wings.

title: The Island That Drags
description: A sea monster of Norse sailors' tales, so large that it was mistaken for an island, until it sank and dragged ships down with its arms. It feeds by releasing a cloud of dung into the water to attract fish. Its death, they said, would foul the sea for miles.

title: The Stone Gaze
description: A mortal woman cursed by Athena into a Gorgon with snakes for hair, whose gaze turns the living to stone. Perseus cut off her head while looking only at her reflection in his shield. Her severed head kept its power, and Pegasus and Chrysaor sprang from her neck.

title: Hunger That Walks
description: In Algonquian folklore, a gaunt, antlered spirit of winter starvation, whose heart is made of ice. Those who resort to cannibalism in the cold can become Wendigos, always hungry no matter how much they eat. The more it eats, the hungrier it grows.

title: The Hunger of Bones
description: A giant skeleton, fifteen times the height of a man, built from the bones of those who died in war, famine or unburied. It walks at night and bites off heads, and a faint ringing in the ear warns that it is near. Sacred charms and Buddhist chants can drive it away.

title: We Are Many
description: A swarm of unclean spirits that lived in a man in the country of the Gerasenes, who lived among the tombs and broke every chain. When Jesus asked its name, it answered 'Legion, for we are many'. It begged to be sent into a herd of swine, which ran into the sea and drowned.

title: The Wheels of Many Eyes
description: Nested wheels of burning topaz, covered in eyes all around their rims, who carry the throne of God in Ezekiel's vision. They roll in any direction without turning, and the spirit of the living creature is in them. To look at one is to be looked at by a hundred eyes.

title: Whose Head Is Carried
description: A headless horseman of Irish folklore on a black horse, who carries his own grinning head like a lantern. When he stops, a soul is called, and any gate opens to him. He drives with a whip made of a human spine, and throws a basin of blood over anyone who sees him.

title: Beast of the Labyrinth
description: Bull-headed son of Queen Pasiphae, kept by King Minos in Daedalus' labyrinth, and fed on tribute from Athens: seven youths and seven maidens every nine years. Theseus finally killed him, finding his way out with a thread from Ariadne.

title: Mother of Monsters
description: Half woman, half serpent, who bore the Hydra, the Chimera, Cerberus and the Sphinx with her mate Typhon. She lurks in a cave in the land of the Arimoi, hating nothing but the light. Zeus allowed her to live, so that her monstrous children could test heroes.

title: The Burning Wheel
description: A flaming ox-cart wheel with a screaming man's face in the hub, which rolls through the streets of Kyoto at night. Legend says it was a cruel governor, reborn as a wheel of fire. Anyone who looks upon the face has their soul torn out, and the only protection is a charm pasted on the door and the shutters closed.

title: The Bronze Sentinel
description: A bronze man forged by Hephaestus, or one of the last of the old bronze race, set to circle Crete three times daily and hurl rocks at invaders. He had one vein of ichor, sealed with a nail at his ankle. When intruders landed, he heated himself red-hot to embrace them.

title: Mask of Burning Jealousy
description: A woman consumed by jealousy until she became a horned demon, her face twisted into the pale Noh mask that bears her name. In the Noh play Aoi no Ue, and the story of Kiyohime, she chases a faithless man to a temple bell and burns him inside. Her mask grows more terrible with each telling.

title: Shadow on the Waves
description: A black giant with a round, bald head like a monk's that rises from calm water and wrecks ships. It appears on still nights, and crews who speak to it are lost. It demands a ladle to scoop water into the boat, and sailors give it one with the bottom knocked out.

title: Maw of the Strait
description: A daughter of Poseidon and Gaia, hurled into the sea by Zeus for stealing Heracles' cattle. Three times a day she swallows the sea and spits it out, creating a whirlpool that no ship can escape. Odysseus survived her only by clinging to a fig tree above the water.

title: Breaker of Rites
description: A tusked, clawed shape-shifter of Hindu myth that haunts cemeteries, breaks sacrifices and eats the dead. He prefers to wear the face of someone you love to lure you out at night. In the Ramayana, the demon king Ravana is their lord.

title: Flayed Rider of the Sea
description: A centaur-like horror from Orkney with no skin, black blood and yellow veins, whose head is ten times too large for the rider's torso. Its breath withers crops and sickens livestock. It hates fresh water, so its only weakness is a running stream.

title: The Earth-Spider of Old
description: An ogre-sized spider of the mountains, spinning webs across a hundred paths. The hero Minamoto no Raikō struck one in his sickbed, followed its blood to a cave and cut it open, and nearly two thousand skulls spilled out of its belly.

title: Boiler of Rivers
description: A demon of disease in Sumerian myth, born of the sky god An and the mountain. His approach is so foul that the fish in the rivers boil alive, and sickness spreads through every land he crosses. He killed warriors by the thousand until the hero Ninurta met him in battle and slew him with his mace.

title: Blue-Faced Cannibal
description: A blue-faced hag of Leicestershire with iron claws, who snatched children from the lane to flay them in her cave, the Bower, dug by her own hands in a hillside. She hung their skins on an oak to dry, and wore them round her waist like a belt.

title: Three-Headed Gatekeeper
description: The three-headed hound of Hades, with a mane and tail of snakes, who lets the dead in and none out. He greeted Orpheus's song by falling asleep. Only one living man ever dragged him into the light: Heracles, as the twelfth labour, who then returned him.

title: Barker of the Strait
description: A nymph transformed by a jealous Circe into a monster with six long necks, each ending in a snarling head, and a ring of dogs' heads at her waist. She lurks in a cave opposite Charybdis and snatches sailors from the decks of passing ships. Odysseus lost six men to her.

title: Lenten Stalker of the Bayou
description: A wolf-headed man who stalks the swamps of Louisiana, the Cajun werewolf. Legend says it hunts those who break Lent, or who fall away from the faith, for a year and a day. Its curse passes to anyone whose blood it draws, and it never sleeps in the sun.

title: Beak Full of Herbs
description: A tall figure in a long waxed coat and a bird-beaked mask stuffed with herbs, who walked through the empty streets of plague-ridden Europe tapping the sick with a cane. His arrival meant a house would be marked and sealed, and behind him the bells rang for the dead.

title: The Host of the Unforgiven
description: The restless dead of Irish and Scottish folklore, the souls of sinners who are barred from heaven. They fly in swarms at dusk from the west, and enter houses through windows to steal the dying. People keep their west-facing windows shut, to keep them out.

title: Risen from the Grave
description: A corpse of Romanian folklore that leaves its grave by night to drain the living, starting with its own household. It rises from those who die unshriven, in sin or under a curse. Villagers drove a stake through its heart, stuffed garlic in its mouth, and burned the heart to ash.

title: Seizer of Fevers
description: A demoness of ancient Mesopotamia, a lion-headed, donkey-eared hag with bird's talons, who brings fever and sickness to mothers and newborns. She suckles a pig and a dog. Only amulets of Pazuzu and incantations turn her away.

title: The Fire That Guards the Forest
description: A giant fire-serpent of Tupi-Guarani legend, born after a great flood when a serpent ate the eyes of drowned animals and became huge, with glowing eyes that never close. It burns hunters and fire-setters who harm the forest, and guards the fields from burning.

title: Night Flyer with a Severed Waist
description: A woman of Philippine folklore who splits at the waist at night, and flies off on leathery wings, leaving her legs behind. She feeds on sleepers, using a long tongue to drink the blood of the unborn. Salt or ash sprinkled on her lower half keeps her from returning.

title: Stench of the Rainforest
description: A giant, shaggy, sloth-like beast of the Amazon with red fur, a hide that turns away bullets, and a second mouth on its belly. Its stench paralyses hunters, and its cry makes them lose all sense of direction. Many believe it is a protector of the forest.

title: The Cart of the Dead
description: In Breton folklore, the Ankou is the personification of death, a gaunt skeleton or a tall man with a wide-brimmed hat and white hair, who drives a creaking cart with a scythe. He collects souls at night. The last person to die each year takes on the role for the next.

title: Riddler of the Cremation Ground
description: A spirit that possesses corpses and hangs upside down from trees in cremation grounds. In the Baital Pachisi, King Vikramaditya carries him on his back while he tells riddles; if the king answers, the corpse flies back to its tree. If he fails to answer, his head will burst.

title: Eater of Mad Minds
description: A flesh-eating, dark-skinned ghoul of Hindu lore, the lowest of the demon classes. They lurk in cremation grounds and deserted places, feed on corpses and drain the minds of the mad. They haunt the sick, the drunk and the dying, and make their victims speak in strange voices.

title: Eater of the Unburied Dead
description: A neighbour by day who works, smiles and goes to market, but by night turns into a dog, a pig or a winged horror to prey on the sick, the pregnant and the newly buried. Garlic, salt and holy objects keep it away. Villages blamed it for every unexplained death.

title: The Bone Whale
description: A skeletal whale that drifts to shore on stormy nights, trailing flickering ghost-fires and rotting, bird-like shapes called hikodama. It is said to be the spirit of a whale killed by hunters. Those who see it on a dark coast fall sick or suffer misfortune.

title: The Smile That Never Leaves
description: A grotesque clown who wanders an abandoned travelling circus, wearing a painted smile beneath a cracked porcelain face. He never speaks and never stops smiling, and he appears wherever children have mysteriously vanished. Those who hear a distant calliope and follow it are not seen again.

title: Lantern of Entrails
description: A floating woman's head with her entrails hanging below, glowing softly in the dark as she hunts for blood. In the Thai tale, she was a cursed noblewoman who practised black magic. She drifts through villages and eats blood from the unwary.

title: The Red Blood-Sucker
description: A pale beauty of Irish legend, forced by her father to marry a cruel chieftain although she loved another. She starved herself to death, and rose from the grave to drink the blood of her husband, her father and any man she could lure. A heavy pile of stones over her grave is said to keep her down.

title: The Whistler with a Sack of Bones
description: A tall, shadowed man of the Venezuelan plains who carries a sack of his father's bones. He killed his father in a rage, and was cursed to carry the bones forever, whistling as he walks. When the whistle sounds close, he is far away. When it is faint, he is near.

title: The Woman with a Hollow Back
description: A long-haired woman in white who wails and giggles in the trees at night, the ghost of a woman who died in childbirth. Her laugh sounds near when she is far, and far when she is near. Her back is hollow, a trail of frangipani scent follows her, and a nail driven into her neck is said to tame her.

title: The Clay Servant
description: A man of clay animated by a holy word placed in his mouth or on his brow. In the legend of Prague, Rabbi Loew made one to protect the ghetto, but it ran wild. He removed the word, and the golem crumbled. He obeys until the word is lost.

title: The Lord of the Lost Path
description: A tall, horse-headed man from the Philippines, with long limbs, who lives in the forest and mountains and leads travellers in circles until they are lost. Wearing a shirt inside out breaks his spell. A person who tames one by tugging on a hair of his mane gains a loyal servant.

title: Eater of the Slain's Hearts
description: A giant raven from Danish folklore that eats the hearts of fallen knights and gains their knowledge. Each time it eats a heart, it grows larger, and it can take human form. It lurks over battlefields, and its cry foretells the death of kings.

title: Barrow-Dweller
description: A Norse corpse guarding its barrow hoard, swollen and cold with the stench of death. Stronger than in life, it rises against thieves, and some can shape-shift or curse the land. Heroes like Grettir had to wrestle them to the ground to take their treasure.

title: The Drowned Maiden
description: The spirit of a young woman who died in the water, usually by suicide or after being betrayed by a lover. She sits in willow branches, combing her green hair, and calls men from the shore with song. They are drowned and entangled in her hair.

title: Bride of the Waterfall
description: A spider that lives for centuries and takes a woman's shape, often waiting by a waterfall or in an abandoned house. She plays a biwa to lure travellers, then wraps them in silk and feeds on them alive. Her spiderlings may swarm from her sleeves.

title: The Iron-Toothed Hanger
description: A creature of Ashanti and Akan folklore who dwells in the forest canopy, with iron teeth and hooked legs. It hangs from tree branches, snagging passers-by with its hooks and draining their blood. It has a human appearance, but its legs bend the wrong way.

title: The Snow Woman
description: A pale woman who walks in blizzards without leaving footprints, and freezes travellers with her breath. In the tale of Mosaku and Minokichi, she spared the young man on the condition that he never speak of her. Years later, he broke his promise.

title: The Monk Who Grows
description: A monk-shaped shadow that appears on dark roads, and grows taller the higher you look at him, until he towers over the horizon. The trick to defeating it is to look down, and say 'I have seen through you'. Then it vanishes.

title: Lurker Under the Duckweed
description: A green-skinned hag of Lancashire and Cheshire with long arms, who hides under duckweed on ponds and rivers. She pulls in children who lean too far over the water, and parents used her name to keep them away from the bank. Her teeth are as green as the weed.

title: The Hopper in the Desert
description: A creature of Arabian lore, a half-man with half a head, half a body, one arm and one leg, who hops through the desert at astonishing speed. It attacks lone travellers and drinks their blood. Some say it is the offspring of a demon and a human, and its flesh is poisonous.

title: Chewer in the Grave
description: A German corpse that chews its own burial shroud in the grave, and every bite drains the life of its family and the village. A plague follows its smacking. To stop it, villagers put a coin or a stone in its mouth, cut off its head, and buried it face down.

title: The Stiff Walker
description: A reanimated corpse in Qing-dynasty official's robes that hops with stiff arms and draws the qi of the living. A paper talisman on its forehead holds it still. It cannot see those who hold their breath. Sticky rice, mirrors or the crowing of a rooster will drive it off.

title: Crouching One at the Bed's Foot
description: A pale, hairless, long-limbed humanoid that crouches at the foot of the bed in the middle of the night. It began as an online tale around 2005, and sightings spread worldwide. It stares at the sleeper without moving, and by morning it is gone, but something has changed in the room.

title: Hair That Keeps Growing
description: A little girl's doll in a kimono that holds the spirit of its dead owner, a girl called Okiku. Her family placed it in a shrine in Hokkaido, where its hair kept growing, and has been trimmed ever since. Its smile is said to widen a little more each morning.

title: Recovery
description: Monarque restores himself. +25 HP, +5 Soul, and every cooldown shortens by 1.
flavor: He pours it out the way one pours for the dead.

monarqueLines.early: I restore what I choose to restore. Continue.
monarqueLines.fraying: Even a fraying king mends himself. Watch.

artDirection: A tarnished-gold chalice tilting over black stone; the liquid is smoke-dark, not red.

title: Burst
description: Monarque breaks his own seal. He loses 15 HP, every other vessel loses 17 HP, and the round ends at once.
flavor: A king who will not be beaten will end the room instead.

monarqueLines.early: The rite ends. Everything ends when I decide.
monarqueLines.fraying: Ruin it all. I will still stand in the ashes.

artDirection: A cracked ring of ash around a single standing figure; fissures run outward through the floor.

title: Reversal
description: The lower stat wins for 2 rounds. Weakness is crowned, and strength is a debt.
flavor: Down is a direction only if someone is still standing on it.

monarqueLines.early: Now the order turns over. Climb, if you can.
monarqueLines.fraying: Down is up. Up is whatever I decree.

artDirection: A black cathedral shown upside down, chandeliers rising like roots, the vessel's shadow upright.

title: Blind play
description: Opponents must play blind this round. They choose a card without knowing which is which.
flavor: The light is not removed. You are merely taken out of it.

monarqueLines.early: Choose without sight. Prove you deserve the light.
monarqueLines.fraying: Darkness suits a throne. Fight blind, vessel.

artDirection: A black disc swallowing a tarnished-gold halo; cards below it drawn as faint outlines only.

title: Insight
description: Monarque reads the vessel: its Soul reserve and its strongest cards. The report is private and expires next round.
flavor: He does not guess. He remembers how this ends.

monarqueLines.early: I see your whole hand. Try to surprise me.
monarqueLines.fraying: I see all of it. Enough to crush you.

artDirection: A single vellum eye bound with iron thread, the pupil a slow candle flame.

title: Boon
description: For 4 Soul, Monarque grants himself one boon: Immortality (no HP damage for 2 rounds), Absolute Power (the card's chosen stat is doubled) or The Unmaking (every opponent loses a card).
flavor: A god's wish costs less than a mortal's, and takes more.

monarqueLines.early: Three wishes lie before me. I need only one.
monarqueLines.fraying: A wish. Mine to grant, and mine to take.

artDirection: Three sealed doors of bone and bronze, one ajar, no light behind it.

title: Sealing
description: A card the vessel played is sealed and removed from play for 10 rounds, with Soul paid by tier.
flavor: What he binds, he remembers how to bind.

monarqueLines.early: Be still. A fallen thing is only a card.
monarqueLines.fraying: Sealed, as I sealed gods. Hold, little vessel.

artDirection: A wax seal pressed into vellum over a card's silhouette, thin cracks already forming.

title: Escalating drain
description: The Unraveling is laid upon a vessel. It drains HP each round and worsens when the holder fails to be rid of it. It may be passed on or broken.
flavor: It is not a punishment. It is what the vessel was always going to become.

monarqueLines.early: It is the mark of the vessel. Carry it with pride.
monarqueLines.fraying: It spreads as I willed. What you are, I can unmake.

artDirection: A thread of grey light unspooling from a hairline crack in a face-shaped silhouette.

title: The Culling Draft
description: Bound beings are laid on the table. The weakest vessel chooses first; each vessel takes one into its hand.
flavor: The bound are cut from the dark like stones. You may take one.
artDirection: Cards laid face-up on black stone, each with a faint silhouette struggling beneath its seal.

title: The Silent Tithe
description: Each vessel secretly offers 0 to 3 Soul. The single highest offer is mended for 15 HP and 2 Soul returned. Every vessel pays what it offered. Equal top offers cancel.
flavor: Name your price in silence. He hears every figure.
artDirection: An iron bowl on an altar, filled with ash and a few pinpricks of light.

title: Rite of the Whetstone
description: Each vessel whets one card in hand for the rest of the match: +40 Power or −5 Rank.
flavor: Each is set against the stone. Something is worn away; something is sharpened.
artDirection: A circular grinding stone of cracked basalt, a card edge held to it, sparks as grey ash.

title: The Debt Called
description: The vessel with the most HP is marked. Anyone who places above the marked vessel gains 8 HP and 2 Soul. If the marked vessel finishes last, it loses 10 extra HP.
flavor: A name is spoken aloud. Whoever owes, owes now.
telegraph: A name is about to be said.
artDirection: A ledger page, one name scored through in tarnished gold, the ink still wet.

title: A Trial Is Set
description: A public task is named for this round. The first vessel to complete it gains 12 HP and 2 Soul.
flavor: A small task, set by a patient hand.
artDirection: A single iron gate half-open on a narrow stair, a candle placed at its threshold.

title: The Hollow Hour
description: Every vessel gains 3 Soul and all cooldowns clear. For 2 rounds, HP lost on placement is multiplied by 1.5.
flavor: The hour empties. What you spend here, you spend double.
artDirection: A stopped hourglass full of ash, the upper chamber already empty.

title: Rite of Exchange
description: The strongest free card of the vessel with the most HP and the strongest free card of the vessel with the least HP trade places.
flavor: Two relics cross the threshold. Neither returns the same.
artDirection: Two cards passing through a narrow doorway in opposite directions, their silhouettes crossing.

title: The Unraveling Laid Upon
description: If no vessel holds the Unraveling, Monarque lays it upon the round leader.
flavor: The seal slips, and the rot finds a host.
artDirection: A hand-shaped fracture crossing a wax seal; grey light seeps from it.

title: The Open Eye
description: The call and every card on the table are visible to all for 2 rounds.
flavor: The candles all turn to face the table.
artDirection: A great vellum eye in the ceiling of a black cathedral, every candle leaning toward the table.

title: The Hushed Crowns
description: Each vessel's best-Power card and best-Rank card fall silent and cannot be played this round.
flavor: The greatest names go quiet. Only the lesser may speak.
artDirection: Two empty thrones, their crowns wrapped in wax and bound with chain.

title: The Weighing
description: No call is made. Power and Rank are weighed together, and the best combined score wins. Balanced beings carry the round.
flavor: A scale is set down. It does not care what you call.
artDirection: A bronze scale with a card on each pan, the beam perfectly level in smoke.

title: The Reversed Hour
description: The lower stat wins this round. The last become first.
flavor: The ladder is turned over. The floor is the crown.
artDirection: A staircase descending upward into a lit doorway, shadows climbing the wrong way.

title: The Boon Round
description: The round's victor is granted a boon: 20 HP, 6 Soul, a being taken from the vessel in last place, or all their cooldowns cleared.
flavor: One of you may ask. The asking has a cost, later.
artDirection: A single open palm held out above a bowl of ash, a thin gold thread rising from it.

title: Debt Doubled
description: All HP won and lost on placement is doubled this round.
flavor: Every wound is entered in the ledger twice.
artDirection: A ledger with each line struck twice, the second stroke in old blood.

title: Desperate Surge
description: The vessel with the least HP plays this round at +100 Power and −8 Rank.
flavor: What is nearly broken burns hotter. Monarque takes note.
artDirection: A cracked card glowing from within along its fractures, tarnished-gold light in the seams.
